title: Use PostgreSQL as the primary data store for root
problem_statement: Document the architectural decision to use PostgreSQL for data-store in root.
context: The codebase contains evidence of PostgreSQL usage in root; see the evidence-refs below. Vendor research was skipped (no_network); the decision relies on in-tree evidence only.

considered_options.name: Continue with PostgreSQL
considered_options.summary: Keep the existing PostgreSQL integration observed in the codebase (see evidence-refs below).
good: Continue with PostgreSQL is documented in primary vendor sources.
bad: Continue with PostgreSQL introduces an additional vendor relationship.

considered_options.name: MongoDB
considered_options.summary: Alternative data-store option to PostgreSQL considered for root.
good: Available as a managed or open-source offering with documented operational guidance.
bad: Requires migration away from the existing PostgreSQL integration evidenced in the codebase.

considered_options.name: Azure Cosmos DB
considered_options.summary: Alternative data-store option to PostgreSQL considered for root.
good: Available as a managed or open-source offering with documented operational guidance.
bad: Requires migration away from the existing PostgreSQL integration evidenced in the codebase.

considered_options.name: Amazon DynamoDB
considered_options.summary: Alternative data-store option to PostgreSQL considered for root.
good: Available as a managed or open-source offering with documented operational guidance.
bad: Requires migration away from the existing PostgreSQL integration evidenced in the codebase.

rationale: PostgreSQL is the technology already integrated in the codebase; switching now would require migration work without offsetting benefit captured in the gathered evidence.

good: Good, because PostgreSQL is already integrated; no migration cost is incurred.
bad: Bad, because the team commits to operational ownership of PostgreSQL (upgrades, capacity, incident response).

confirmation: Static check: every component in root resolves the PostgreSQL client at build time.
Lint check: configuration keys named in this ADR remain referenced from the codebase (CI grep gate).
Smoke check: an integration test exercises a representative read and write through the documented client.

diagram.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    participant root as root
    participant Cache as Application cache
    participant Store as PostgreSQL
    root->>Cache: read
    Cache-->>root: miss
    root->>Store: query
    Store-->>root: rows
